html:
A plot in 63 BCE by the senator Lucius Sergius Catilina, known as Catiline, to seize power in Rome after he lost the election for consul.

Catiline was a patrician deep in debt who had done well under Sulla. Beaten in the elections of 64 and 63 BCE, he gathered other indebted nobles and Sulla's ruined veterans, and an army formed in Etruria. The consul Cicero learned of the plot through informers. In the four Catilinarian Orations he denounced Catiline before the Senate and the people, starting with the famous "How long, Catiline, will you abuse our patience?"

Catiline left Rome to join his army. Letters given to envoys of a Gallic tribe, the Allobroges, exposed the plotters left in the city. In the Senate debate Julius Caesar argued for life imprisonment and Cato the Younger for death. Cato won, and five men were strangled on 5 December 63 BCE without trial. Catiline died fighting at Pistoria early in 62 BCE.

Cicero saw it as his finest hour, but the executions got him exiled in 58 BCE. The historian Sallust wrote a short book on the affair.
sum: A plot in 63 BCE by the senator Lucius Sergius Catilina, known as Catiline, to seize power in Rome after he lost the election for consul.
